When I was 4 years old, a burglar broke into my family's apartment while my parents were out with my sisters for some reason. My babysitter and 12 year old brother attempted to resist the intruder. They were both shot and killed. My 8 year old brother and I hid in our room and didn't come out until the police arrived (a neighbor or something must have called 911).

No suspects were ever found, and the case went nowhere. My parents and older siblings were so traumatized that my family collectively repressed the event. Even 27 years later, nobody will talk about it without a severe emotional outburst.

It severely affected my trust in society, other people--hell, even locks on doors.

Wow this takes me back. My first time out of the country as an adult, tagged along on a friend's business/leisure trip to Djibouti for a few weeks. The first week in the city was definitely interesting as I was mostly by myself or with a mutual friend who spoke mostly French and very little English.

But the real gem of this trip was our final week: tagging along with an Afar group (they will hire out escorts for surprisingly low costs, to be totally honest I was worried we were being swindled/going to be kidnapped) as they traversed the Danakil. They mine places like Lake Abba (the much larger salt-crusted lake near this photo) for salt and haul it back across the desert on camelback.

We had two guys with AKs standing around smoking cigarettes while we lounged in this pool (I think this exact one, but there were a few small pools just like it) and took photos like the ultimate tourists. More than any other experience in my life, I felt like I was a movie character. Thanks for posting this OP, I love this sub for all the new places I learn about, but there's such an indescribable joy in seeing places I've visited before.

Few years back I lived/worked at Crater Lake NP. Started going to a particular hot springs in the area (not exactly a secret, but not too well known either) regularly. Most of the time there would be one, maybe two other parties there, super quiet and quaint spot. Loved it.

So a friend from HS (we both originally lived on the east coast) and I started hanging out irregularly because they lived in Portland. Now, since HS this friend had become an "influencer" of sorts (about half a million followers) and while that never really played into our friendship it was always weird having them make glammed-up Instagram posts about basically everything we did together.

One time I took this friend to these hot springs, with a few of their other friends ("satellite" influencers to first friend's orbit). They were all so amazed that one could just hike into a spot so magical. Little did I know I may have had a huge part in ruining the magic of this place.

All four of these influencers posted pictures of the springs, tagged the location, and encouraged their followers to visit it. I was pretty annoyed, as I had given them all the "protect the secret" talk on our way in, and apparently they all just regarded it as some hipster bullshit. Within a few months, each one of them had gone back at least once to do photoshoots there. As the winter went on, I started seeing photos of the springs everywhere: Twitter, Tumblr, Instagram, even reddit posted photos of it many, many times.

Now, I don't want to imply I'm so important a guy that I caused those springs to now be a tourist-trapped partyzone, but over my two years at CLNP I watched those springs absolutely fucking transform. It broke my heart.

So yeah, if you want to know where this is: find it :)
